subject: Logic
title: Why Proofs Matter
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Why Proofs Matter.

hook.text: Science can be overturned by a new experiment. A mathematical proof, once verified, stands forever.

buildup.text: A proof is a chain of logical steps that shows a statement must be true, not just probably true.

discovery.text: Unlike evidence, proof offers certainty. Two plus two will still equal four a billion years from now.

twist.text: That's why math is called the queen of sciences—its truths don't expire, decay, or need replication.

climax.text: Understanding proofs means understanding what it means to know something beyond any possible doubt.

quiz.question: How does a proof differ from scientific evidence?
options: Proofs can be overturned by experiments
Proofs establish certainty, not just probability
